title: Sort loans without mutating Redux state
contract: Implement sortLoans(items, sorting), returning an array ordered by sorting.field (loanAmount or applicantName) and sorting.order (asc or desc). Never mutate the input array or loan objects. Keep original relative order for equal values. Compare numeric amounts numerically and names lexicographically using ordinary JavaScript string ordering. Inputs are frozen.
hints: Array.sort mutates the array it receives. Copy the array before sorting.
A comparator must return zero for ties; equal values should keep their original order.

tests.name: Frozen state sorts by numeric amount ascending
tests.explanation: Copying the array avoids mutating the frozen store; equal amounts remain stable.

tests.name: Descending amounts keep stable ties
tests.explanation: The comparator must handle equality in either direction.

tests.name: Names sort in descending string order
tests.explanation: Select the requested field rather than always sorting amounts.

tests.name: An empty list is valid
tests.explanation: No special mutation or fabricated record is needed for empty input.

tests.name: Amounts are compared numerically, not as strings

businessContext: A developer copies array references using shallow array methods (`const items = state.items; items.sort(...)`), mutating the frozen state in place or returning a new value while also mutating draft state in Redux Toolkit.
productionSymptom: Runtime error: `TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property of object` in production builds, or Redux selector listeners fail to notify components of changes.
